analysis.title: The 720: Global Memory, Kioxia, CXMT, Japan SPE, Foxconn II, Victory Giant, HKEx downgrade, ASEAN Banks, Mizuho, US Internet
key_insights: Global Memory: GS stays constructive on 2027 on AI memory demand but is more measured on 2028 given AI capex sustainability, muted consumer demand and higher China supply. 2028E conventional DRAM and NAND price forecasts cut to -19% and -21% YoY.
HBM TAM estimates for 2026E-2028E raised to US$60bn-US$237bn on significantly higher ASPs. Operating profit estimates cut 23-26%.

Samsung Electronics (Buy, on CL) TP cut to W350,000 and SK Hynix (Buy) TP cut to W2,000,000. GS argues current prices discount zero 2028 AI capex growth and an additional 40% ASP decline versus base case.
CXMT (Buy): TP cut to Rmb99 from Rmb131 as DDR5 mass production starts. 2027-30E earnings cut 18-27%, and 2027-28E revenue sits 9-11% below consensus on an expected DRAM correction.

Kioxia (Buy): TP cut to ¥21,000 from ¥39,000 as GS factors in gradual NAND price decline from April-June 2027. FY3/28 and FY3/29 operating profit cut 15% and 30%, with 100% surplus FCF return policy supporting a 30%+ shareholder return yield in FY3/28.

Japan SPE: GS prefers Lasertec, Disco, Ebara and Tokyo Electron, and is cautious on SCREEN, Tokyo Seimitsu and Ulvac. Sector EV/EBITDA multiple cut to 12X from 18X on growth deceleration risk from FY28, with Lasertec TP cut to ¥52,000 and Disco to ¥72,000.
Foxconn Industrial Internet (Buy, TP Rmb106): AI server racks ramp from 4Q26, with CPO switch demand and ASIC server exposure driving 2027 growth.
Victory Giant (Buy, TP Rmb540): AI PCB spec upgrades drive capacity expansion, with improved yields and stronger 4Q26 profitability. Equipment installation is the main constraint.
Hong Kong Exchanges downgraded to Neutral from Buy, TP HK$433 from HK$514. IPO conversion has slowed and FY27-29E ADT estimates cut 11-12% and EPS 7%, with consensus EPS at downside risk.
Westlife Foodworld downgraded to Sell from Neutral, TP raised to Rs600 from Rs560. Wage inflation and food costs pressure margins, EPS cut 4-5% and EBIT up to 6% below consensus.

China data centers: Alibaba lowered its FY28 cloud growth outlook to 30-45% YoY and said its 20GW capacity target by end-2032 could be reduced. GS sees slower capex as positive for GDS and VNET leverage and FCF, and prefers integrated AIDCs like Range.
China Semis: local AI chip market seen at US$678bn by 2030E, and China WFE revenue to grow 20% YoY to US$53bn in 2027E with local supplier exposure at 38% by 2028E.

ASEAN banks: ASEAN data-center exposure concerns are seen as overdone. China-linked AI workloads are 15-25% of ASEAN live demand and lending to pure-play operators is 0.1-0.4% of loans for DBS, OCBC and Standard Chartered.
Korea insurance: GS prefers Buy-rated SFM for dividend capacity and is Neutral on DBI and HMF. TPs are cut after a risk-free rate update to 3.9%.
Mizuho FG (Buy on CL, TP ¥11,000): CEO cites a personal 16% medium-term ROE view, a ¥150bn structural cost cut plan, and lower rate sensitivity of ¥100bn from ¥120bn.

US Internet: 3Q26 capex across Amazon, Google, Meta and SpaceX exceeded $170bn. Cloud backlog is above $1.1tn, with AWS growing 39% YoY and Google Cloud 103% YoY. Amazon, SpaceX and Uber are highlighted as compelling risk rewards.
Amazon (Buy, TP $370), Alphabet (Buy, TP $385) and SpaceX (Buy, TP $245) were all reiterated. SpaceX trades 39% below its post-IPO peak.
US Strategy: the S&P 500 is down 12% from its October 6 record high. GS names three bottoming conditions: AI earnings confidence, a better macro backdrop, or a major positioning decline.
Rates and FX: risk-off has undone much of the hawkish front-end repricing. USD/JPY is near 160, where MoF intervention risk rises, and GS favors short EUR/JPY.

earnings_insights: US Internet 3Q26 reported: aggregate capex across Amazon, Google, Meta and SpaceX exceeded $170bn.
AWS revenue growth accelerated to 39% YoY in 3Q26 as reported, and Google Cloud revenue grew 103% YoY. Management expects AWS revenue growth of 40% or more in 2027 and 2028.
GS expects Alexa for Shopping to generate about $16bn revenue in 2026E, up 33% YoY (GS estimate).
HKEx: GS cuts FY27-29E ADT estimates by 11-12% and EPS by 7%, and sees consensus EPS at downside risk.
Westlife Foodworld 2QFY27: GS cuts FY27-FY29 EPS estimates by 4-5%, with EBIT estimates up to 6% below consensus.
Kioxia: GS cuts FY3/28 and FY3/29 operating profit estimates by 15% and 30%.
Mizuho 1H26 results briefing: non-interest factors drove about three-quarters of the recent upward guidance revision, and the full-year expense ratio is expected in the low 50% range.
Korea insurance 3Q26: underwriting recovery was overshadowed by investment valuation losses, and GS cuts 2026E-28E estimates by 3-4%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Sell-off broadened from AI unwind to growth downgrade.
MoF intervention likelihood increases near this level.

risk_factors: AI capex sustainability, with a scenario of zero 2028 AI capex growth.
Muted consumer demand for smartphones and PCs, plus rising China DRAM and NAND supply.
Deeper challenges to the AI trade could drive markets to price durably higher policy rates.
Growth deceleration risk from FY28 for Japan SPE.
Equipment installation and production-line readiness constrain Victory Giant demand conversion.
Slower ASEAN project conversion could temper loan growth for Singapore and Hong Kong banks.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund net leverage has declined to its lowest level since April 2025.
GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator remains elevated, with $170bn of mutual fund and ETF inflows since the start of 4Q26.
Mutual funds and hedge funds have substantial overweights in Health Care, Industrials and Financials, and recently added Consumer Discretionary while cutting Communication Services.
geopolitical: New US restrictions on China-linked AI compute are driving concerns over ASEAN data-center exposure and may accelerate China client migration to local supply chains.
Possible Japanese MoF intervention if USD/JPY approaches 160.
China-linked AI workloads represent 15-25% of current ASEAN live demand.
